/LILIAN

Baltic Exchange Market Report - 25 November 2026
Baltic Dry Index: 3107 (39)
Baltic Capesize Index: 5014 (72)
Baltic Panamax Index: 2223 (44)
Baltic Supramax Index: 1814 (3)
Baltic Handysize Index: 1079 (2)

CAPESIZE
The market continued to make positive progress today, although the pace of gains in the Pacific slowed compared with recent sessions. The BCI 182 5TC increased by a further $656 to close at $45,473. In the Pacific, the C5 index edged up just $0.065 to $16.150, with sentiment remaining positive but rates showing only modest improvement. Three C5 miners were active alongside solid operator demand. Offers opened in the $17s before easing into the mid-to-high $16s as miners initially held back. This ultimately resulted in a number of fixtures being concluded in the very high $15s by one miner, while the other two reportedly paid around $16.00-$16.10 levels. An operator was also understood to have fixed, although details of the rate remained undisclosed. In the Atlantic, activity remained limited in the South, with an early C3 fixture reported at $35.10 for 21–23 December arrival, while $35.50 was also heard. Towards the close, there was talk of $36.00 being achieved for 17 December cancelling, although details remained vague. The C3 index edged up $0.068 to $35.259. The North Atlantic maintained a firmer tone, with C8 adding a further $1,661 to reach $45,094. Overall, another positive day for the Capesize market, with the Pacific consolidating recent gains while the North Atlantic continued to provide support.

PANAMAX
The Panamax market saw increased activity across both basins, with the P5TC rising by $398 to $20,009. In the Atlantic, brokers reported stronger mineral and grain demand for trans-Atlantic business while available tonnage continued to tighten, particularly off the West Mediterranean. This encouraged owners to raise their offers for both trans-Atlantic and fronthaul trips as they sought to test higher levels. Although fronthaul activity remained comparatively subdued, firmer sentiment and a tightening tonnage list continued to support improving rates. In the Pacific, market participants reported further signs of improvement, with an increase in fresh enquiry accompanied by a reduction in prompt tonnage availability. In the north, brokers noted renewed grain demand from the North Pacific, with charterers reportedly improving their bids and fixtures being concluded above previously reported levels. Australian rounds also showed signs of strengthening, with healthier cargo volumes encouraging owners to raise their expectations. Meanwhile, Indonesian activity remained relatively limited, with owners seemingly reluctant to commit to shorter duration employment amid concerns that vessels would become available again in mid-December which has meant bid levels had to increase in order to attract interest.

SUPRAMAX
With many travelling to Geneva for parties, the market had a lacklustre feel, but the 11TC average was up slightly to settle at $22,925. The North Asian routes posted positive returns for the first time in a while, whilst the Indian Ocean continues to struggle with little fresh demand evident, but there was not much in the way of fixtures or rumours emanating from the East. In the Atlantic, the Mediterranean remained quiet with few trades emerging and a softer outlook, whilst the Continent remained firm with an Ultramax fixed from Immingham in the low $34,000’s to cover an EMR stem, and the Flag Filia (56,519 2014) open Algeciras said to have fixed delivery passing Gibraltar for a trip via Dordrecht and Rotterdam to Iskenderun with scrap at $26,000 with Pangaea. North America remained active, with rates holding up at strong levels with the Melinda (57,981 2012) open Brownsville 2nd December said to be on subjects basis deliver SW Pass for a trip EC Central America with agriprods at $24,000 with Lauritzen and the Aviona (56,898 2011) open Puerto Limon being placed on subjects delivery SW Pass for a trip NC South America with grains at $24,000 to Weco. The Kiran America (56,666 2010) was rumoured to have failed basis delivery US East coast for a trip UK-Continent with woodpellets at $30,000 with Norden, who then took the Ultramax mv Charlie instead, and XO were linked with the Obi Island (63,543 2025) open New Orleans 6th December on subjects for a trip Egypt with coal at an impressive $42,500.

HANDYSIZE
The market delivered a mixed performance today, with some regions holding steady while others recorded stronger gains. The BHSI rose by 8 points to 1,062, while the 7TC average increased by $148 to close at $19,114. Across the Continent and Mediterranean, the market remained broadly flat, with rates holding around previous levels. Meanwhile, the South Atlantic saw a slowdown in activity and a slight easing in rates. In contrast, the US Gulf maintained its upward momentum, supported by firmer bids and offers that signalled improved confidence. Across Asia, activity remained limited although some tightening of tonnage was noted in the North Pacific, with rates slightly above last-done levels.

Atlantic
The Eva Master (40,242 2022) open Liverpool 24-28th November fixed on voyage terms via Gdansk to Turkey with scrap by Glencore, but further details were not disclosed. A 34,000-dwt open in the West Mediterranean on 4–6 December heard fixed for a trip via the Continent to the East Mediterranean with scrap at $20,500, although further details were not disclosed.

Asia
A 40,000-dwt open in North China on 27–29 November was fixed for a trip to the Continent at $21,250, although further details were not disclosed.

Market Fundamentals
Mosaic Extends Brazil Phosphate Shutdown
Mosaic is extending the temporary shutdown of its Uberaba phosphate plant and Tapira and Catalão mines in Brazil, with no restart date set, CRU reports. The company cites tight supply and high prices of sulphur, a key raw material. Uberaba has capacity of 0.9 Mtpa of MAP and TSP, while Tapira and Catalão produce around 1.8 Mtpa and 0.9 Mtpa of phosphate rock respectively. This follows a partial production curtailment at some Brazilian and US sites in May and further cuts in early July.
